description:
Lightweight, private Windows system monitor.

Vitals shows what is slowing your computer down, in plain language: CPU, GPU, memory, disks,
network, temperatures and per-process usage, with history, alerts and a compact overlay.
Optional read-only access from your phone on the local network. No account, no telemetry.
The watch app fits round watches. In short:
- Wear OS: every screen fits a round watch, small or large, with nothing cut
  at the edge — the reason Google Play turned the watch app down.
- Live lists stay still between updates.
Fixed
- Wear OS: no text or button is cut by the edge of a round watch any more.
  Google Play's review turned the watch app down on 2026-10-19 because the
  first card, the "No PCs yet" text and the sensor rows touched the bezel.
  Each reading is now its own row, so rows narrow as they reach the top and
  bottom of the screen instead of one tall card riding the curve; lists start
  and end where Material 3 recommends for a round screen; explanations and
  empty-state text are centred and kept to the middle of the display; the
  small ring on the home cards sits in the middle; long names end in "…".
  Checked on small round (192 dp), large round (227 dp) and square watches,
  at the largest font and in Romanian, by a test that fails when any line of
  text or any button crosses the display.
- Live lists stay still. On Performance, a reading that comes and goes
  (CPU power or temperature, GPU power, Wi-Fi signal) keeps its place and
  shows a dash while it is missing, so the other figures no longer jump from
  one cell to another every second; the same holds for temperatures and fans
  on Thermals and on the Dashboard. On the AI page, agent cards, queues, jobs
  and per-project rows keep their places while the figures update, and still
  move straight away when an agent starts or stops working (otherwise the
  list re-sorts every 30 seconds). The Processes table, the Dashboard's top
  programs, Network and the phone's process list re-sort every few seconds
  instead of on every update. Nothing moves while the pointer is over a list
  or the keyboard focus is inside it, so a row never slides away from a click.

Verifying this download
Windows may show a SmartScreen warning on first run (Windows protected your
PC) because the installer is not yet signed with a commercial certificate.
Choose More info → Run anyway. That is expected — see
docs/distribution.md.
You do not have to take our word for what is in the binary. With the
GitHub CLI:
gh attestation verify .\Vitals_x64-setup.exe --repo dragoscv/vitals
This proves the file was built by this repository's release workflow from the
tagged commit, and nowhere else. Checksums for every file are in
SHA256SUMS.txt:
(Get-FileHash .\Vitals_x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
Software bills of materials (CycloneDX) for the Rust and JavaScript
dependencies are attached as sbom-rust.cdx.json and sbom-js.cdx.json.
